nodes.summary: Concepts to borrow from the MCP code-graph field, tiered by fusion with unique assets. Tier 1: diff-aware test impact (Covers edges backward from git diff), MinHash similarity shortlisting for the prover (makes the section-12 pairwise sweep tractable), measured-coverage import (closes reachable-vs-asserted caveat), graph_diff tool, content-hash incremental indexing + syntax-only fast tier (solves fast per-commit C# nesting). Tier 3 synthesis: plan -> SurgicalEdit -> prover-verify closed loop. Not borrowed: cloud, language breadth, vectors.

2026-08-07 survey of the MCP code-graph field. Unique to RazorGraphTool: the flow-equivalence prover as refactoring gate, and Razor/PageModel/JS cross-boundary correlation. Near-unique: coverage-as-reachability (one other implementer: roslyn-codelens-mcp, the closest competitor - watch it). Commodity: call graphs/references/impact. Field is ahead on language breadth, incremental indexing, vector search, token economy, composable queries. Strategy: invest in prover + Razor to stay distinct; incremental indexing + Lua to catch up. Added 2026-08-09: Modelcode.ai (Morph) as the process-wrapper pole - enterprise migration service that independently rediscovered the Janet shape (spec-first, milestone gates, compounding project knowledge) but whose correctness story is behavioral sampling only, because cross-language migration has no shared compiler model. Validates verification-as-product; does not close the prover gap. Feeds note.razorgraph-cross-language.

The operating skill for the RazorGraph cluster: WHEN to reach for the graph (questions text search cannot answer - callers, implementers, blast radius, test reach, nesting, flow equivalence) and the workflow (build once/save/load, orient then drill, direction semantics, exact m:Type.Name(params) ids, coverage=reachability, body tools for method-level, mechanical refactor gates, source only to spot-check). Judgment here; depth delegated to the linked nodes; blind spots on note.razorgraph-mcp-server.

Census the population; the anomaly announces itself. When one instance will not explain itself, classify every instance you can reach and sort by frequency -- over-representation is counted, not deduced, and needs no theory of the bug. Corollaries: the classifier must be a marker present on EVERY member (the byproduct nobody can turn off), and absence is a finding (a count of zero is invisible to instance inspection). Origin: a WinINet leak found by running a per-object vtable type-recovery extension across the whole heap and tallying -- thousands of copies of one structure, turning "memory is growing" into a type name and therefore an owner; the vfptr is the only self-describing marker in a native C++ heap, which managed devs later got as !dumpheap -stat. WHEN: memory growth with no obvious owner, a dump that will not explain itself, a query returning suspiciously empty results, any "I do not know what I am looking for" moment -- count first, inspect second.
caveats: The census is only as honest as its classifier: a marker that non-polymorphic types (or unextracted node kinds) lack will undercount silently, which produces the absence-as-finding trap in reverse -- a zero that means "not classifiable" rather than "not there". State what the classifier can see.

nodes.summary: Command-line twin of RazorGraph.Mcp over the same Core+Extractor engine (D:\Repos\RazorGraphTool\src\RazorGraph.Cli). Six commands: build (one project; a .sln needs --project), build-solution (spans every project - the only source of cross-project edges), query (--id/--type/--uncovered/--deep/--mismatches/--escapes), body and body-diff (compile the project, emit a method CFG / prove two bodies flow-equivalent, exit 0 equivalent 1 different 2 error), research (relevance-scored subgraph). Matters because it has NO publish cycle: dotnet run sees the change you just made, while the MCP server reports on the last .mcp-bin publish - so the CLI is the only surface that can observe RazorGraph while RazorGraph itself is being changed, and CLI-vs-MCP disagreement is expected mid-development.
caveats: query mode precedence is silent and fixed (mismatches > escapes > uncovered > deep > id > type): pass two modes and the earlier wins with no warning the other was ignored. --deep 0 is gated on Deep > 0, so it is indistinguishable from not passing --deep.

The research command defaults -o to research.json IN THE CURRENT DIRECTORY. Run it from D:\Repos\JanetHome without -o and it overwrites the Janet research graph - the file the never-hand-edit rule protects. Unrelated file, same name. Always pass -o.

build <sln> --project Foo and build-solution <sln> are different graphs, not two spellings: the former uses the solution only for context and yields no cross-project Calls/Covers edges, which reads as missing data rather than the wrong command.

Output is human text, not the Janet JSON envelope - query has no --json flag; only body and body-diff emit JSON and research writes a file. Use Search-Json.ps1 against the saved graph for scripted queries. --uncovered caps its listing at 200 (reported, not silent).
body and body-diff do not read a saved graph: they run a real compile every invocation, like build/build-solution. Only query and research load JSON and are fast.

Property/Field gap RESOLVED at cd12114 (2026-08-08): prop:/field: nodes (statics included), Reads/Writes edges, and member->declared-type References edges are emitted by builds from source. Saved graphs built before cd12114 still hold zero member nodes, and the published .mcp-bin serves the old extractor until re-published - the CLI/MCP disagreement this note predicts is live right now.

build-solution gained --no-tests (20ff394, 2026-08-08): skips test projects BEFORE compiling (detection by test-framework metadata references), reported on stderr and in output, never silent. Coverage query modes (--uncovered, --covering-tests, --covered-methods) now exit 1 with an explanation on ANY test-less graph - including single-project builds, which previously returned empty coverage silently. The refusal is the report.
